g1.label: 1. The flat is far ___ small for four people.
g1.why: Far too + adjective: far makes too stronger.

g2.label: 2. The room isn’t big ___ for two desks and a bed.
g2.why: Enough follows the adjective: big enough for.

g3.label: 3. There is more than ___ space for a desk and a sofa.
g3.why: More than enough + noun means a lot more than needed.

g4.label: 4. The seminar is ___ good to miss.
g4.why: Too good to miss: too + adjective + to-infinitive.

g5.label: 5. He speaks ___ quickly for most of us to follow.

g6.label: 6. She was ___ tired that she fell asleep during the seminar.
g6.why: So + adjective + that-clause shows the result.

g7.label: 7. It was ___ a long journey that we booked a hotel.
g7.why: Such + a + adjective + noun, then a that-clause.

g8.label: 8. I haven’t got ___ money to pay the deposit.
g8.why: Enough comes before a noun: enough money.

g9.label: 9. We received ___ complaints about the noise to ignore them.
g9.why: Complaints are countable, so use too many.

g10.label: 10. The library is ___ to work in, but the chairs are uncomfortable.
g10.why: Quiet enough: enough follows the adjective.

g11.label: 11. The lecture was ___ less interesting than I had hoped.
g11.why: Far + less + adjective modifies the comparison strongly.

g12.label: 12. At that moment she ___ the contract, so we waited outside.
g12.why: At that moment describes an action in progress: past continuous.
